analysis.title: The NVIDIA affair brings Trump and Xi closer
key_insights: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO on about 12 November amid a US national-security probe into chip diversion to China, then was reinstated on 23 November, eleven days later. The author says the affair has drawn Trump and Xi closer rather than breaking the détente.

At the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Xi reaffirmed the 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' and the two sides agreed to draft an action plan. Bessent said H200 sales policy to China is unchanged, and Trump suggested Blackwell chips could be sold to China in two or three years.

Trump owns the H200 decision, and a collapse of the détente would support critics who say chips were given away for nothing. Xi needs the 'back door' of licensed, smuggled or rented NVIDIA compute to train frontier models until China's own AI stack can stand alone.

The back door is narrowing. A US Commerce rule effective on the summit day requires a licence for any data centre worldwide giving Chinese-headquartered firms large-scale access to advanced AI compute.

The two administrations diverge from the leaders. Commerce is tightening controls, both parties back chip-export restrictions in the 2027 defence bill, and the Democrats take control of Congress from January. The AI Overwatch Act would let lawmakers block sales to adversaries.

Commerce approved 879,868 NVIDIA H200 and equivalent AMD chips for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, including firms on the Pentagon's Chinese military companies list, according to records released by Rep. Brian Mast.
NVIDIA's share of China's specialised AI hardware market fell from 95% to zero as Beijing steered firms to Huawei. NVIDIA chips are allowed only when strictly necessary, for training advanced models.
Huang's return comes with governance limits. NVIDIA's board set up a national security and export control committee of independent directors and is hiring a chief compliance officer.

The trade truce expires on 10 January and the leaders meet again at the G20 in December. Beijing's retaliation tools are rare-earth licensing, paused but not dismantled, and a faster shift to Huawei Ascend chips.

Europe is a bystander exposed on two fronts. Its AI factories depend on NVIDIA, its industry on Chinese rare earths, and the new US rule could restrict its access to advanced US chips if Chinese firms trained models in European data centres.

market_movers.rationale: Huang was reinstated on 23 November with Trump's backing, but under a new export-control committee and a compliance officer. China share is already zero and US export curbs are tightening.

sector_views.rationale: Leader-level support for H200 sales contrasts with tightening Commerce and Congress controls, and China is shifting to Huawei.

risk_factors: Trump-Xi truce expires on 10 January with no confirmed extension.
China could reimpose rare-earth controls, which would also hit Europe.
Congress could remove chip-sale decisions from presidential control.
Evidence of smuggling or remote access abuse could turn the H200 policy into a political liability.
Further export tightening on data centres abroad could hurt NVIDIA and compute access in Europe.
geopolitical: Trump-Xi third meeting of 2026 at APEC in Shenzhen showed no rupture and agreed to draft an action plan.
The US-China trade truce expires on 10 January and the leaders meet again at the G20 in December.

A new US Commerce rule requires licences for data centres worldwide giving Chinese-headquartered firms large-scale advanced AI compute access. Beijing threatened countermeasures but did not spoil the summit.
China's rare-earth export controls were paused after the 2025 Busan APEC summit but not dismantled, and could be reimposed.
Congress is moving to codify chip export curbs in the 2027 defence bill and the AI Overwatch Act.

tension_points.bull_case: The NVIDIA affair made the leaders co-dependent. Trump needs the relationship to justify H200 sales and Xi needs the back door, so both avoided a rupture at Shenzhen.
tension_points.bear_case: Commerce and Congress are tightening controls regardless of the leaders. Beijing could retaliate with rare-earth licensing and a faster shift to Huawei, and the bargain makes each leader a hostage of the other.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Expiry of the trade truce on 10 January without an extension, or China reimposing rare-earth controls.

theme_stances.key_argument: The NVIDIA affair has made the two leaders more dependent on each other, though administrations and Congress keep tightening controls.
